title: The Dead Village
timelinePosition: Directly after Chapter 2's close: the party walks into Millhaven at the last of the light, at the supper hour, on the day after the arrest. Verifier timeline: B1-B4 run from last light into full dark; B5-B6 at night; B6a is the night hold; B7 at first light; B8-B11 in the early morning and on into the day's ride south. Chapter 4 opens two days later.
openLocation: Millhaven, first human village south of the Quel'Thalas borderlands
transport: Mounted approach on Thalassian horses; on foot during the village sweep
immediateObjective: Sweep Millhaven, learn what happened to its people, and decide whether the threat is moving toward Quel'Thalas.
constraints: Absolute limited third on Sylvanas; nothing she could not perceive or infer
Jaina stays 'the mage' in Sylvanas's narration for the whole chapter (partnership-arc marker); she does not grow warm, she just stops treating the read as optional
Open on silence and procedure, not another fight (Ch 2 closed on three violent or dread beats)
No confirmation that grain carries the sickness: the granary reads loudest and Jaina refuses to treat it as the answer
No proof of an organized cult behind it; dead moving north is a direction, not a command structure
The old carter reads as ordinary, useful and forgettable; Sylvanas builds no case around him or his farewell
The grain-seller mention is a weak, unresolved clue: heard once, not connected
Second read of Beat 9 is plant only; the prose must not explain it
Keep consistent with Ch 2 B11: the deer was wounded and still on its feet, not reanimated; the sickness is active in living flesh before death
Fatigue registers for both women after a ride with no sleep
Neral and the unnamed ranger leave the book's southbound party at Beat 8; the survivor girl never continues south
Lyriel's carter answer is warm and true and must not sound careless

Arrival is at last light, not midday (Ch2 prose: 'the last of the light', 'the hour for supper'). The outline's 'stopped in the middle of the day' and 'tools that should have been touched that morning' describe when the villagers' life stopped, not the hour the party arrives.

Elves cannot feel the contamination directly (memory: world/magic). Every 'wrongness' Sylvanas registers must come through the horses, the silence, the staff, the mage's words or the frost on the mage's hand. Her bare-palm reading belongs to ward-stones only.
The dead did not march up the stretch of road the party rode in on in Ch2. The north-northeast line leaves Millhaven another way and cuts toward the ward line, not the Pass gate (see B7).

Ch2 images are callbacks, not discoveries: the mill wheel, the race, the inn sign, no smoke and no dogs (crest and walk-in), and the bowls left on the table (the Ch2 farm, which Sylvanas got from Cyndia's report).
The unnamed escort ranger is 'the fourth ranger' in Ch2 prose and memory. Their gender is not established, so keep them ungendered.

worldbuildingReferences: stories/the-plague-road/locations/lordaeron-and-northrend.md (border country, Millhaven: crossroads, mill, tavern, a few dozen lives)

povKnowsAtOpen: The contamination is real and big enough to matter beyond one village
Jaina's magical read is useful even when her sense of the physical road is weak
Millhaven is the first place on the south road where the wrongness knots tight
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: How the sickness first got into the village
Whether the dead are moving with purpose
How large the threat is beyond Millhaven
mustNotBeImpliedYet: Any confirmation that grain carries the sickness
Any proof that an organized cult is behind it
Any hint that the old carter is anything but a useful local source
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Millhaven is the first village on this road fully taken
The survivor girl's testimony and the tracks confirm the dead marched north toward Quel'Thalas
Neral rides north with the survivor and the warning; only Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia and Lyriel continue south
A newer grain seller has been mentioned once, as a weak unresolved clue
Lyriel answered the carter's grain-seller question; on a first read it is nothing

pov: She opens treating this as a border problem to read and report, not a human disaster she has to carry herself.
The silent village and the missing bodies force her to read tracks, corpses, and magic together.
She starts the chapter using Jaina as a specialist, not a partner.
By the end, Sylvanas still does not trust Jaina, but she stops treating the mage's read as optional.

beats: Sylvanas expects Jaina to be good at magic and weak on the actual road.
Jaina proves more useful than that by helping separate the loudest wrongness from the real pattern.
Sylvanas does not grow warm, but she starts listening when Jaina speaks.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They begin as a custody escort with no trust between them.
Millhaven forces them to build one picture out of physical and magical evidence.
They do not soften. They just stop wasting time pretending the other half of the problem does not matter.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: remains with the riding party. She is the ranger Sylvanas trusts most on the ground.
Lyriel: remains with the riding party. She talks to anyone on a road, and she is the one who answers the carter.
Neral: present at open. She rescues the survivor girl and rides north with the warning dispatch in this chapter.
Unnamed escort ranger: rides north with Neral and the survivor girl.
Survivor girl: found in a cellar. Escorted north by Neral. Does not continue south.
Old carter: helpful local source on the road. He should read ordinary, useful, and forgettable.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 4 opens after a two-day ride south with Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia, and Lyriel.

A survivor girl from a cellar was sent north
Neral carried the physical warning dispatch back to the border
The southbound party is stripped down to exactly Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia, and Lyriel

scenes.title: Millhaven
scenes.sceneFunction: They enter the first village the plague has truly emptied and realize the missing dead are the real problem.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The contamination is real and the party arrives at Millhaven after a ride with no sleep, but they still don't know how it got here. Ch 2 showed it active in living animals before death. Sylvanas holds Jaina as a specialist, 'the mage', not a partner.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas defaults to physical procedure and her own training; Jaina's magical read has to earn a place beside it.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only: Millhaven is the first alarm-bell village, crossroads, mill, tavern, a few dozen lives, doors open and people gone (lordaeron-and-northrend.md); border country is mud, grey-green woods, livestock, woodsmoke, autumn harvest. Thalassian horses are trained to tolerate ward hum and settle fast, so a horse that will not settle is itself a signal (thalassian-horses.md). No web research run; no canon source for Millhaven's layout beyond these notes, so mill, well, granary and cellar placement is planner inference.

beats.goal: Enter Millhaven and secure it by procedure: read the silence, set a perimeter and order a full physical sweep before anyone relies on the mage's senses.
beats.conflict: Nothing to fight and nothing to see. No voices, animals or work sounds; the wrongness is thick enough to unsettle trained Thalassian horses; the party is tired and every closed door could hide a living thing or a bad surprise.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas gets her sweep ordered and the party deployed in pairs, but the village gives up no danger and no answer, only the sense that it stopped mid-day.

beats.valueShift: border problem to read -> something her training has no drill for
newOnPageInformation: Millhaven is silent, not burned or sacked; the stop is recent
The horses spook at the wrongness
Sylvanas orders a physical sweep first, magic second
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether anything alive is still hiding inside

beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: the sweep begins and the first houses will show how the village stopped
beats.timeAnchor: Last light, the supper hour, on the day after the arrest.
beats.continuityNote: Ch2 already gave the mill wheel standing still, the water on the race, the inn sign, no smoke, no lights and no dogs, so these get one callback anchor. Millhaven's smell is not yet established and is open. Horses: Ch1 and Ch2 established that ward-bred horses sidestep once at a stone and then stand, and that they clench up outside the rings. Spooking here escalates that, and Sylvanas reads it as a signal. The custody terms from Ch2 still hold: the mage rides in the middle, keeps her hands in sight and does not step off the road unless Sylvanas puts her off it.
continuityCorrections: Outline 'stopped in the middle of the day' and 'that morning' describe when the villagers' work stopped. The party arrives at last light (Ch2), so the beat must not set the arrival in daylight. Planner's 'tools that should have been touched that day' was replaced with 'tools left mid-task'.
beats.povNote: This is the first time we are inside Sylvanas since Ch1. She has not been shown reacting to the culvert, the map or the doe, so her interior picks up from the facts she holds (memory: knowledge) without a recap of the ride. Elves cannot feel the contamination; the wrongness must reach her through the horses, the silence and the mage. Arc bullets 1 and 3 anchor here: a border read, with the mage as an instrument.
beats.verifierModification: Settled the timeline (planner flag): the arrival is at last light. Upgraded one sensory anchor and marked the Ch2 images as callbacks. Normalized the transition label.
beats.plannerWarningResolved: Timeline flag resolved by the verifier: last light, into dark. See timelinePosition and B6a.

beats.goal: Find the dead or the kill site: bodies, blood, a stand point, any reading of how the village fell.
beats.conflict: There is nothing. Every house shows people leaving the middle of ordinary life and not returning; the village emptied slowly, not in one panicked attack. No bodies to study means no wounds, no cause and no count.

outcome.summary: No kill site, no corpses, and three bad possibilities (fled, taken, or rose and walked out); Sylvanas has nothing physical to read, so Jaina turns to the places that hold the most magic.

beats.valueShift: expectation of a massacre -> a puzzle without a body
newOnPageInformation: No pile of bodies and no clear kill site anywhere in the village
The village emptied over time, ordinary life frozen in place
One barn cat walks the street unbothered
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether villagers fled, were taken, or rose and walked out
sensoryAnchors: half-eaten food gone stale on tables
wooden toy dropped on the floor
barn cat moving unbothered
made beds, open shutters
fatigue behind the eyes
beats.transitionIntent: planted question: with no bodies there is nothing physical to read, and the only instrument left is the mage
beats.interiority: Sylvanas has seen sacked towns; this is not that. A town does not simply stop. Keep the cat in mind: animals that are fine, people that are gone. She is counting what is missing, not what is there.
beats.plannerWarning: Ch 2 B11 established the plague active in animals; the barn cat's health is ambiguous. Write it as plainly ordinary, healthy-looking and indifferent, not a sign of immunity or pattern.
beats.continuityNote: Sylvanas got the Ch2 farm from Cyndia's report at the stirrup: door on the latch, bowls on the table with a spoon in each, the child's coat on the peg, the cart gone south toward Millhaven. Millhaven is the same pattern at village scale, so the stale food on the tables should register as the farm again, multiplied, not as the first time she has seen it. Whether the farm family's cart reached Millhaven is open; do not settle it. On the cat: Ch2 put the sickness in deer and wolves, but the rooks were unbothered and the horses read clean, so the cat is plainly ordinary.
beats.verifierModification: Marked the stale-food image as an evolution of the Ch2 farm (anti-reintroduction). Beat weight set to light: the sweep should be compressed. Normalized the transition label.

beats.goal: Get Jaina's reading of the most saturated sites (well, cellar, granary, soil) while Sylvanas holds the sightlines, and find the source of the sickness.
beats.conflict: The whole village is soaked and the loudest site does not mean the first one. The granary reads strongest of all, but Jaina refuses to call the loudest residue the whole answer; to Sylvanas, that restraint could be caution or performance.

outcome.summary: Magic shows the scale and the saturation, but no clean origin; Sylvanas notices the mage's discipline and begins, a little, to trust her judgment, while still needing tracks to know where it went.

beats.transitionIntent: planted question: the scale is known and the route is not, so Sylvanas takes the search out behind the village to read the ground
beats.interiority: expected a scholar to grab the loudest answer and call it proof; the mage did not, and that is irritating; is it caution or a performance for the Ranger-General; one granary is not enough, and she would have said the same
beats.plannerWarning: Grain must not be named as carrier. The granary is loud and Jaina declines to crown it. Sylvanas must not conclude 'grain'. Jaina's refusal should read as method, not a hidden theory.
beats.continuityNote: Ch2 set up this read precisely. Jaina wanted to go deeper at the crossing to test source against sink: thickest at the crossing and thinning evenly along every line means it is rising there; lines that disagree in weight and lag mean it is draining in. Sylvanas answered 'Then I pick the ground.' Clearing the sightlines around her is Sylvanas picking that ground. The outline's result: saturation everywhere, the granary loudest, no clean first source. The source-or-sink test must not come back with a clean answer, so the millhaven-source-or-sink thread stays open (the 'fully taken' end state is about the people, not the origin). The frost cost escalates and does not reset: her right hand has been dead since the frost-sheet in the ambush, and she read the doe with her left. Whichever hand she reads with, Sylvanas sees what it costs (frost a hand's width round the palm, going grey, skin peeling). Cyndia already reported the frost in Ch2, so it is known, not a first sight.
beats.povNote: Sylvanas cannot perceive the read itself. The mage's restraint about the granary has to reach her as something said or done in front of her: her words, the staff, the frost, her face. This beat starts throughPov Jaina bullet 2 and partnership bullet 2.
beats.verifierModification: Tied the beat to the Ch2 setup (the deep read at the crossing, 'Then I pick the ground', the frost cost) so it reads as a payoff, not a fresh idea. Added the POV filter. Normalized the transition label.

beats.goal: Read the ground behind the village and call the direction the dead went.
beats.conflict: The earth is churned by drag marks and ruined lanes; too many uneven feet over each other for a clean line; Cyndia cannot get a count; Sylvanas refuses to guess or overstate.

outcome.summary: Many dead left on their feet, but the trampled ground gives no clean direction and no number, and without a witness the mess stays a mess.

beats.valueShift: confidence in procedure -> honest refusal to guess
newOnPageInformation: Many of the dead left Millhaven on their feet
The road behind the village is too trampled for a direction call

beats.transitionIntent: planted question: no direction without a witness, so the search turns from the ground back to the houses and cellars for anyone alive
beats.continuityNote: This is the first on-page evidence that the villagers left on their feet after death. The nearest precedent Sylvanas holds is the Ch2 doe, which kept running after a heart-shot, but the doe was alive and wounded, not raised. She may set the two against each other; she must not equate them. It is full dark by now, which is one more honest reason she will not call a direction. Cyndia's tracking (deer slots and wolf pads in one track at the holly) is established, so her attempt at a count uses the method we have already seen.
beats.verifierModification: Added a time anchor and the Ch2 doe boundary. Normalized the transition label.

scenes.title: The Survivor and the Proof
scenes.sceneFunction: They find a living child in the wreck of the village and turn horror into physical proof they can send north.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: It is full dark. The village is dead and the bodies are gone; the dead left on their feet but no direction is certain. They still need proof of where the threat moved next, and they don't yet know whether anyone is alive.
scenes.arcPressure: The physical evidence and the magical read have to be combined into one picture; this is the scene where Sylvanas lets the mage strip noise from the ground.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only: Neral is the early third ranger and northbound dispatch rider, structural use is getting warnings out and escorting the survivor (supporting.md); voice sheet governs her manner. Plague notes: dead rise at death after repeated ingestion and answer as a 'choir', crude convergence, rough answerability (plague-mechanism.md), which supports 'rough formation' without a commander. No web research run. The 'at least sixty' count is the outline's number, not sourced.

beats.goal: Get the hidden child out of the cellar alive and calm enough to speak, without frightening her back into the dark.
beats.conflict: She is dehydrated, terrified and barely able to speak; she trusts only Neral; the cellar is cramped and the party is unsure whether anything else is down there with her.

outcome.summary: The girl is alive and confirms people died here and something happened at night, but she is fragile and her memory may be broken.

People died here and something happened at night
Neral is the one ranger the girl instinctively trusts

Sylvanas never heard that thought, so the payoff is the reader's, not her knowledge. castAndHandoffRules give the rescue to Neral, so Neral must be the one the girl comes out to; the outline also puts Jaina in the cellar, and both can be there. Neral's established manner is the low Thalassian murmur she uses on frightened horses. Her voice sheet bars therapist language.
beats.povNote: Sylvanas stays above the hatch (planner). However the girl is first detected, Sylvanas must perceive it or be told it. The fourth ranger and Lyriel hold the perimeter.
beats.verifierModification: Made Neral's rescue role explicit (handoff rule) and noted the Ch2 closing-question payoff. Normalized the transition label.
beats.plannerWarningResolved: POV kept above the hatch (carried into povNote).

beats.goal: Pull a usable account from the girl: what happened, when, and which way the dead went.
beats.conflict: She remembers pieces, not a narrative; terror may distort route and order; Sylvanas will not accept a child's word as proof without the ground matching it; Jaina has to separate fear from the useful magical detail.

outcome.summary: Fragments line up: sweetness on people's breath, sick neighbors, the dead rising and dragging north at night, and a newer grain seller mentioned in passing; the pieces point north, but terror might be bending the route.

beats.plannerWarning: Do not make the grain-seller a clue anyone pursues here. Plant it as a line the party weighs for a moment, then sets aside. Sweetness on breath is a symptom reported, not a mechanism confirmed. Avoid the word 'bread' or any grain-carrier reading.
beats.continuityNote: Neral's voice sheet includes a sample about who brought the flour to the house. If a household-food question is used, it stays a household question and nobody connects it; the grain-seller mention is the girl's, weighed once and set aside. 'Sweetness on the breath' is a symptom she reports, not a mechanism. The girl's 'north road' is her own word for the way they went; B7 must reconcile it with the ground.
beats.povNote: The mage sorting terror from useful detail has to be audible to Sylvanas (a question, a correction, a remark), not narrated from inside Jaina.
beats.verifierModification: Retargeted the transition into the added B6a night hold: the planner's 'Sylvanas goes to check the road cut' ran straight into the dark.

beats.emotion: Fatigue past tired into a flat clarity; the border pulls at her, and all she has to send is a child's word she cannot check in the dark.
beats.dilemma: Send the warning north tonight on a frightened child's account, or hold it until first light lets her read the road cut and send something she can stand behind.
beats.decision: She holds the warning for the light, sets the watch and keeps the party in the village overnight.

beats.continuityNote: Fatigue: Sylvanas has been up since the morning troll sweep in Ch1, through the night ride and the day's ride; Jaina has been awake since before her pre-dawn crossing. A promise is owed from Ch2: Jaina said she wanted to check the horses again 'tonight', and Sylvanas answered 'You will.' The writer may pay it here. If shown, the result does not change (the horses read clean), and do not introduce sickness in the horses.
beats.povNote: Agency beat for Sylvanas in a scene where Neral and the mage carry the work. The hold is her call. B6 already establishes that she demands the ground match the testimony; this beat stages that decision.
beats.verifierModification: Added. Ch2 lands the party at dusk. Outline B7's track work needs daylight, and B9's carter needs an ordinary daytime road, so the night has to be crossed somewhere between B6 and B7. Without this beat the writer faces an unmarked 8-10 hour jump in the middle of a scene. It also gives a sequel slot after the B5 peak and a place for two nights without sleep to register. No new plot, character or location; the decision comes from B6's 'Sylvanas still demands the ground match it'.

beats.goal: Verify the girl's account against the ground, and put numbers and a direction on the dead.
beats.conflict: The tracks are damaged and the magical noise confuses the physical read; Cyndia starts out skeptical; a wrong call would send a false warning to Quel'Thalas.

outcome.summary: The ground confirms the girl: at least sixty bodies moved north-northeast toward the border in rough formation, turning the threat into a direct border warning; but nothing explains what raised them or who leads them.

beats.valueShift: doubt -> alarm, with the warning finally solid

The threat is now a direct border warning, solid enough to send

beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: the warning is real, so it has to ride now
beats.plannerWarning: Ch 2 constraint: no organized undead column. 'Rough formation' here is bodies walking the same way in a crude press, not trained ranks; keep it consistent with the plague-mechanism 'choir' (crude convergence, no handler proof). Do not suggest a commander. Also the outline's '60' is a floor, not a final count.
continuityCorrections: Geography: in Ch2 the party rode the road down from the Pass to Millhaven (culvert, farms, holly bend, crest) and met no column. Cyndia read tracks on that road at the holly and found only deer and wolves. So the dead did not march up the stretch of road the party rode in on. The north-northeast line has to leave Millhaven another way (a lane, a field track, or off the north road before the farms; where exactly is the writer's call) and cut across country toward the ward line, not the Pass gate. Sylvanas should register that they did not ride through it. The girl's 'north road' can be a child's name for the way they went. This fits silvermoon-thread Ch9, where Millhaven's dead are burned on the border runestones.
beats.continuityNote: Sylvanas reading with bare fingertips follows her established habit of pulling the glove off her right hand for stones. Here she reads the edges and depth of the grooves, not magic; elves cannot feel the contamination. The mage's part is to tell her which marks read as the dead and which as living animals or carts, so the physical count comes out of the noise. That is where throughPov Jaina bullet 2 and partnership bullet 2 land; the specifics are the writer's. 'Rough formation' means bodies walking abreast in a crude press (the 'choir' in plague-mechanism), not ranks, and no commander.
beats.verifierModification: Added the route correction: the dead could not have used the road the party rode in on. Moved the beat to first light. Retargeted the transition from 'tonight' to 'now'.

scenes.timeAnchor: Night, through to first light at the road cut (B7).

scenes.title: The Old Carter on the Road
scenes.sceneFunction: Sylvanas sends the warning north, crosses paths with a casually helpful old carter, and commits her remaining force to riding south.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: First light. The ground at the cut confirms the girl: at least sixty dead moved north-northeast toward the border. The survivor has to leave now with the dispatch, and Sylvanas has to weigh the border against the south.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas chooses the border over her own comfort and then chooses to keep following Jaina's trail rather than fall back; she tells herself it is the trail, not the mage.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only: the carter is the Mal'Ganis plant (investigation-arc.md; lyriel-voice.md fixes her answer: she tells him they passed nobody, mentions the girl's grain-seller, says they will watch for him going south, and that he would get a better price going home full). Cyndia hears the odd farewell here and again in Ch 15 as independent corroboration (cyndia.md), so she should be within earshot. Lordaeron border country is farmland, mud, livestock, harvest (lordaeron-and-northrend.md). No web research run. Mal'Ganis's identity and the downstream consequences (Ch 5 depot, Ch 9 ward) are plant-only in this chapter and come from project notes, not canon.

beats.emotion: Tight, cold urgency: the theory has become a cellar, a child and sixty feet of ground, and she resents how much of this is now hers to carry.
beats.dilemma: Keep the full escort and risk the dispatch arriving late, or strip her own force to guarantee the warning and the child reach the border.
beats.decision: She sends Neral north with the girl, the dispatch and the extra escort, cutting her own strength to four for the ride south.

beats.continuityNote: In Ch2 Neral was named the relay and planned to change horses at the Pass and keep going. She rides a bay and leads the spare grey ('fresh legs for the climb back'; the tooth-score on its near hock read clean), so the grey is the natural spare for the northbound pair. The outline's 'extra escort' is the one fourth ranger. Convocation: Ch1 left Lor'themar covering the budget session, and he has been off the page for two chapters. chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch2 ends in Jaina's POV at the last of the light. From the crest Sylvanas orders 'Bows in hand. We walk them in. Cyndia, the left. Lyriel, the right. Mage, in the middle, and you stay there.' They go down at a walk, knee to knee between the garden walls; the hooves ring on the stone at the bottom of the hill; the inn sign creaks on its bracket at the crossroads. Jaina's last thought: was there anyone, one person, anywhere in all those houses?
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Same moment, same formation, POV handed to Sylvanas. Neral is behind with the spare grey and the fourth ranger holds the rear. Both leads have gone without sleep since before the arrest; Jaina's right hand has been dead since the frost-sheet in the ambush, and she is sick with the old-coin taste. The doe, the ruled-line closure at Millhaven and 'Then I pick the ground' all happened yesterday.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: This is the first time the reader has been inside Sylvanas since the Ch1 cell. She still holds the noon stone (late beat, cold under the warmth) and the circle on the map; Jaina does not know either. Jaina's question about whether anyone is alive was never spoken aloud, so Sylvanas does not know it. Her own reading of the ride (the culvert, the doe, the map) has only been seen from outside and is hers to carry in now without a recap.

craftResearch.findings: Slow pacing makes anxiety where fast pacing makes adrenaline. Linger on small wrongnesses and withhold the explanation, because a reason given early kills the dread.
Bury the true clue among ordinary detail, and don't let the sleuth dwell on one item longer than the rest. A fair clue is visible on the page but not signposted.
Use simple open questions and avoid 'why', which puts a child on the defensive. A child in shock needs comfort before questions, and her memory comes back in fragments, not in order.
A sequel runs reaction, dilemma, decision and turns the last scene's disaster into the next scene's goal. Its length sets the pace, and a sequel can be a single paragraph.

pacing.notes: Tension: medium build through S1 (B1-B3), disaster at B4, peak at B5 (the child), dip at B6 and the B6a night hold, second peak at B7 (sixty north), then a long release in S3 with an undertow under the carter. No run of 3+ high beats. Every scene has four beats, so length varies by weight instead. S1 runs medium because B2 is light and the sweep is compressed. S2 is the long scene (B5, B6 and B7 full). S3 is short to medium, with B8 and B10 light and B9 full. Per the dread research, S1 can linger on small wrongnesses, but B1 and B2 must not both play the same note (emptiness): B1 is silence and horses, B2 is what the houses hold.

structure.notes: The opening picks up mid-motion from the Ch2 walk-in. The mid-chapter turn is B5 (beat 5 of 12, 42%): a living witness turns a sweep into questioning. The close turns on an unresolved question: Sylvanas's self-deception ('the trail, not the mage') and a next village alive enough to misread itself. Scene/sequel is 8/4 after the B6a addition, against 8/3 from the planner. That is about right for an investigation chapter with action peaks. Outline beats 11 map to plan beats 11 with no merges, plus one verifier sequel.

character.notes: Sylvanas acts in every beat: she orders the sweep, picks the ground, refuses to guess, holds the warning, reads the cut, strips her own force, takes the road read and chooses south. B5-B6 lean on Neral and the mage, and B6a gives her the decision in that stretch. Supporting roles are distinct: Cyndia counts and hears the farewell, Neral handles the child and the relay, Lyriel is the warm voice that answers the carter (background in S2), and the fourth ranger holds the perimeter. POV risks are fixed with notes: no elf sensing of the contamination (B1, B11), Jaina's restraint and sorting must be audible (B3, B6), Sylvanas stays above the hatch (B5). Every arc bullet lands (arcLandingMap).

transitions.notes: B8's 'empty places in the line follow into the meeting' pointed at gaps that do not exist until B10 (Neral is present in B9), so it was rewired as an action continuation. B7's 'ride with it tonight' clashed with the daylight track work and was retargeted. B6 now hands into B6a, and B6a hard-cuts to first light. All labels are normalized to the pipeline set. Scene boundaries hold: B4's need for a witness lands in B5, and B7's warning lands in B8.
